name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q01 - Centripetal sequence of tissue layers in dicot stem

questiontext.text:
Identify the correct centripetal sequence (from the outer periphery to the center) of the given anatomical layers in a transverse section of a young dicotyledonous stem:

  1. Hypodermis
  2. Epidermis
  3. Pericycle
  4. Endodermis (starch sheath)
  5. Pith

Select the correct sequence from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the outermost protective boundary
The outermost layer of the primary stem body is the epidermis, which forms a continuous single-cell thick protective layer covered by a waxy cuticle and bearing trichomes.

Step 2: Identify the sub-epidermal cortical zone
Directly below the epidermis lies the hypodermis, consisting of a few layers of collenchymatous cells that provide mechanical flexibility and strength to the young stem.

Step 3: Identify the innermost cortical boundary
Following the middle parenchymatous cortical layers, the innermost boundary of the cortex is the endodermis, whose barrel-shaped cells store dense starch grains and constitute the starch sheath.

Step 4: Identify the perivascular and central tissues
Interior to the endodermis lies the pericycle in the form of semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above the phloem of vascular bundles, and occupying the central-most core is the parenchymatous pith.

Step 5: Conclude the centripetal arrangement
Tracing from the exterior periphery toward the central core, the tissues occur in the order: Epidermis (II) → Hypodermis (I) → Endodermis (IV) → Pericycle (III) → Pith (V).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANATOMY_OF_FLOWERING_PLANTS_MCQ_Q02 - Sequence of layers traversed in dicot root

questiontext.text:
If a micro-probe penetrates a primary sunflower (dicotyledonous) root radially from the exterior toward the central pith, arrange the anatomical layers and tissues in the correct sequential order of encounter:

  1. Endodermis with Casparian strips
  2. Epiblema with root hairs
  3. Pericycle
  4. Parenchymatous cortex
  5. Conjunctive tissue and primary vascular bundles

Choose the correct sequence from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the external starting surface
The outermost boundary layer of a primary dicot root is the epiblema (rhizodermis), whose tabular cells give rise to unicellular root hairs for absorption.

Step 2: Determine the intermediate cortical zone
Beneath the epiblema lies the extensive cortex, comprising multiple layers of loosely arranged, thin-walled parenchymatous cells with intercellular spaces.

Step 3: Determine the endodermal barrier
The innermost layer of the cortex is the single-layered endodermis, characterized by barrel-shaped cells with suberin-impregnated Casparian strips on their radial and tangential walls.

Step 4: Determine the stelar components
Immediately interior to the endodermis lies the pericycle consisting of thick-walled parenchymatous cells. Further inward lie the alternating radial vascular patches embedded in parenchymatous conjunctive tissue, finally enclosing a small or inconspicuous central pith.

Step 5: Conclude the radial penetration sequence
The chronological sequence encountered from outside to inside is: Epiblema (II) → Parenchymatous cortex (IV) → Endodermis with Casparian strips (I) → Pericycle (III) → Conjunctive tissue and primary vascular bundles (V).
